transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I suppose what finally got me to come in is that over this past year or so, I just feel like I’m constantly in motion. I’m 87, so you’d think I’d be better at sitting quietly by now, but I’m always puttering around—fixing little things, arranging things, straightening something that probably doesn’t need straightening, or saying yes to one more volunteer task when I already have enough on my plate.

It’s not that anything dramatic happened, exactly. It’s more that I’ve noticed I have a very hard time just sitting down and being still. Even when I tell myself, “Now just sit and rest,” before I know it I’m up doing something else. It’s started to feel a little… I don’t know, tiring, I guess, and hard to ignore.
Do unwanted thoughts keep popping into your mind and make you feel like you have to do these tasks?

Hmm… I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I don’t think it’s like a thought pops in and frightens me or nags at me until I do something, if that’s what you mean. It’s more… I’ll notice something, or remember something small, and then I’m just up doing it before I’ve really decided anything.

Like, I don’t sit there thinking, “Oh no, I must straighten that or something terrible will happen.” It’s not like that. At least I haven’t noticed that kind of feeling. It’s more automatic, I suppose. I see a thing out of place, or I think of a little task, and my body seems to get there before the rest of me has had a chance to say, “Leave it alone and sit down.”
During these periods when you’re constantly moving, do you also feel unusually cheerful or high?

Unusually cheerful or high? Hmm… I don’t think so. Not in the way that sounds, anyway. I mean, I can be in a perfectly decent mood while I’m doing things, or even feel pleased if I’ve gotten something tidied up, but I wouldn’t say I feel “high” or especially cheerful all of a sudden.

It’s more like I’m restless and pulled along by the doing of it, if that makes sense. Sometimes I’m even a little annoyed with myself because I wanted to sit down and rest, and there I am up again fussing with something. So no, I haven’t really noticed a special happy or elevated feeling going along with it.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things?

I don’t think I worry a lot, no. I mean, I worry the normal amount, I suppose—appointments, whether I remembered to do something, little practical things—but I wouldn’t say I sit and stew over things all day.

Sometimes I’ll think, “Oh, I should take care of that,” and then I’m up doing it, but it doesn’t feel like worry exactly. It’s not a heavy anxious feeling, at least not that I’ve noticed. It’s more that I get pulled into doing things before I’ve really settled myself. But everyday worrying… no, I don’t think that’s the main thing for me.
When you were a child, were you already someone who had a hard time sitting still?

Oh yes, I think so. I mean, looking back, I was that child, definitely. In grade school I was always being told to sit down or stop popping up out of my seat. I can still remember teachers saying my name in that tone, you know, like they’d just barely gotten me settled and then I was up again.

And I talked over other children too, not to be rude exactly—I don’t remember meaning to be rude—but I’d get excited and just start speaking before it was really my turn. I was told I was “too lively” quite a bit. That was the phrase people used then, or at least the one I remember. This was well before I was a teenager, so it wasn’t just some adolescent thing. It was there pretty early, from what I remember.
Over this past year, have you often felt down or depressed?

Down or depressed… no, I don’t think I’ve often felt that way this past year. I mean, I have ordinary low moments, like anyone my age probably does—days where I’m tired or a bit fed up with myself—but I wouldn’t describe it as being depressed, not really.

It’s more that I get restless or irritated with how I’m spending my time, if that makes sense, but not a deep sadness hanging over me. I haven’t noticed a pattern of feeling down most of the time. So I’d say no, not often.
